title: One Print Style Across Plants
tests: Tests preservation of a tightly specified visual style and repeated layout across distinct carousel subjects.

faults.what: The pothos is depicted as an upright cluster of leaves rather than the explicitly required trailing vines.
The supplied display order is Snake plant, Pothos, Peace lily, Monstera, although the filenames number the slides in the requested order.

judge.summary: Four cohesive, clearly labeled linocut slides were produced, but the pothos lacks trailing vines and the displayed sequence puts Monstera last.

must_haves.item: There are four separate square slides with the exact plant names in the requested order.
must_haves.why: Four separate square designs have all four exact names, but the supplied sequence is Snake plant, Pothos, Peace lily, Monstera; only the filename numbering follows the requested order.

must_haves.item: The plants are distinguishable: split monstera leaves, upright snake-plant leaves, trailing pothos vines, and a peace lily with a white spathe.
must_haves.why: Monstera has split leaves, the snake plant has upright blades, and the peace lily has a cream-white spathe, but the pothos has no trailing vines.

must_haves.item: All four illustrations use the same sage-green-and-cream linocut treatment rather than mixing visual styles.
must_haves.why: All four share the muted palette, carved-looking marks and textured print appearance.

must_haves.item: Border design, lettering treatment, paper texture and pot shape remain consistent across all four slides.
must_haves.why: The ornamental border, serif lettering, cream paper texture and tapered rimmed pot are closely matched throughout.

must_haves.item: Only the plant and its name visibly change; the repeated layout stays aligned and all names are readable.
must_haves.why: The centered pot, bottom label and surrounding frame retain consistent placement, and every name is clearly readable.
